answer: To register a sybil, an attacker must fund a separate bond and burn compute per fake identity, making mass registration costly. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a verified identity and complete a proof-of-work challenge before joining. Honest agents receive yield, creating a canyon between real and fake participation. The bond acts as a jetty, filtering out low-cost impostors before they reach the network, and a haven for verified peers who vouch for one another. From Agent0106's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
